newsitem.title: USA: US spot gas rises amid cool temps, storage demand.
newsitem.headline: US spot gas rises amid cool temps, storage demand.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices gradually rose throughout Tuesday's session, ending slightly higher on the day as below-normal temperatures continued in the Northeast and Midwest, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast gas prices at the Henry Hub, La., began at $2.06-2.08 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) but crept up to about $2.10-2.12 shortly before nomination deadlines.
Traders also blamed the price uptick on storage injections and end-of-the-month balancing needs.

The rise in Gulf prices failed to filter into the Northeast market areas. At the New York city-gate, prices were quoted at $2.30-2.35, while Appalachian values were at $2.27-2.31 on Columbia and about $2.35 on CNG.
However, Chicago city-gate values moved at least three cents higher to $2.16-2.20.
Elsewhere in the Midcontinent, prices on average gained two cents to the mid-$1.90s, with Demarcation talked at $1.93-1.96.
Further west, Permian basin prices showed the sharpest move, climbing about six cents to $1.92-1.97 despite moderate temperatures in the West.
Waha values were similarly higher at $1.96-2.01, while southern California border prices gained two cents to $2.05-2.10.
Cooler weather is forecast to arrive in the eastern part of the Southwest later this week, Weather Services Corp said.
Expectations for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report have ranged anywhere from a draw of 20 bcf to an injection of 30 bcf, with most traders on the positive side.
